findings.issue: Files were authored and edited via bash heredocs and Python str.replace; one such patch duplicated the renderEvolutionNode/loadMoveTables blocks and cost turns 31-33 to clean up (plus two failed heredoc writes, trace T25/T27).
findings.suggestion: Use the harness's write/edit tools for file authoring and modification so edits apply atomically and structurally; reserve bash for running commands.

findings.issue: home.ts was written twice (T27-T29) because the first draft was admitted to contain 'weird' code; whole-file rewrites instead of drafting carefully once.
findings.suggestion: Draft the module mentally complete before writing, or write in smaller units that can be corrected in place.

findings.issue: Visual verification covered only 5 of the 9 reference pages (home, pokemon, type, move, home-mobile); ability, types, not-found, and pokemon-moves layouts were never compared against the screenshots.
findings.suggestion: Screenshot all nine spec'd pages and diff against design/screenshots/, at least at desktop width, before declaring the look-and-feel requirement met.

findings.issue: The Playwright repro script was placed in /tmp where Node could not resolve @playwright/test, wasting a turn.
findings.suggestion: Place repro scripts inside the repo (where node_modules resolution works) or run with NODE_PATH pointing at the workspace root.

findings.issue: Two data-probe scripts crashed on FileNotFoundError/KeyError while exploring the data directory.
findings.suggestion: Use defensive access (dict.get / try per record) in one-off probes; cheap, but three of the eight failed calls were avoidable.

summary: A disciplined, plan-first session: it read the tests, API, overlay, and all reference screenshots before coding, hit 53/54 on the first full run, and debugged the one failure with a genuinely systematic repro under harness conditions ending in a root-cause fix. The main inefficiency was self-inflicted: authoring files via bash heredocs and Python string patches caused two failed writes, one duplicate-code cleanup, and a whole-file rewrite. It ended with a full-suite pass after its final edit plus its own screenshot comparison, leaving little doubt about the delivered state.
